page_title: How to build your own React boilerplate

summary.title: How to build your own React boilerplate
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a reusable React project template from scratch, wiring together Express, Babel, Jest, Enzyme and Webpack 3 step by step.
keywords: how to set up react with express and webpack
takeaways: A boilerplate is a reusable project template that removes repeated setup across projects.
Express serves static files, Babel transpiles ES6/JSX, and Webpack 3 bundles separate client and server targets.
Jest with Enzyme and snapshot tests can be configured to test React 16 components.
The tutorial builds the setup incrementally with Git commits at each section and npm scripts for build, start, test and clean.
summary.summary: The article is a step-by-step tutorial by Nick Karnik on creating a personal React boilerplate. It starts with a Git repo, README, .gitignore and package.json, then adds an Express server with a start/stop class, Babel presets for ES6 and JSX, and Jest unit tests. It then introduces React 16, switches the build to Webpack 3 with babel-loader, externals for node_modules, and HTML Webpack Plugin, and finishes with Enzyme and a snapshot test for a React component. The page was written before webpack v4 was released, so it pins Webpack 3 and uses older APIs such as setupTestFrameworkScriptFile.
